panels.description: Processes per group by state. Waiting/Other/Zombie are usually 0; any Zombie series is an incident signal (parent not reaping).
panels.title: process states

panels.description: Age of the oldest process in each group; a step to 0 means the group restarted. Groups with unreadable start time (year-0001 sentinel) are filtered out.
panels.title: uptime (oldest process)

panels.description: Largest fraction of the fd limit used by any process in each group. Normalized against the limit: 90% of a small limit is more dangerous than 5% of a big one.
panels.title: fd pressure (worst ratio)

panels.description: Faults per second that required disk I/O. Sustained rate above 0 is a real problem (thrashing, cold caches).
panels.title: major page faults

panels.description: Voluntary = the process chose to sleep (I/O wait, futex); non-voluntary = preempted or timed out (CPU contention).
panels.title: context switches

panels.description: Ten hottest threads across the selected groups. Thread data is only exported for groups the exporter can introspect (see appendix).
panels.title: top 10 threads by cpu

panels.description: Per-thread I/O needs /proc/<pid>/task/<tid>/io, readable only by the owner or CAP_SYS_PTRACE. With a non-root exporter most series stay zero — see the spec appendix "Making sparse panels dense".
panels.title: top 10 threads by io

panels.description: CPU split into user vs system time; a high system share means kernel-bound work (syscalls, page faults, locks). Row kept collapsed by default so the panel does not load until expanded.
panels.title: cpu by mode (user/system)
